questions.stem: Koch's postulates cannot be fulfilled for Mycobacterium leprae. Which postulate fails?

options.A: The organism is present in every case of the disease
options.B: The organism is isolated in pure culture in vitro
options.C: The organism reproduces the disease in laboratory animals
options.D: The organism is re-isolated from the infected animal
options.E: The host produces specific antibodies to the organism

questions.explanation: M. leprae cannot be cultivated on artificial media, so pure culture (postulate 2) fails. A: It is present in every case. C: Failure in lab animals is the N. gonorrhoeae exception (human-only disease). D: Re-isolation is not the stated problem for M. leprae. E: Antibody production is not one of Koch's four postulates.

questions.stem: Bacterial mesosomes are functionally analogous to which eukaryotic structure?
questions.explanation: Mesosomes are invaginations of the bacterial cell membrane carrying respiratory enzymes, so they replace mitochondria (which bacteria lack). A: Bacteria lack a Golgi. B: Lysosomes are digestive organelles, not respiratory. C: Bacteria lack ER. E: Bacteria have their own (70S) ribosomes; these synthesize protein, not energy.

questions.stem: Protein-synthesis inhibitors can be selectively toxic to bacteria because bacterial ribosomes are:
questions.explanation: Bacteria have 70S ribosomes (30S + 50S); human cells have 80S (40S + 60S), so drugs can target one without the other. B: That is the eukaryotic (human) ribosome. C: 40S is a eukaryotic subunit. D: 30S and 50S form the 70S, not 80S, ribosome. E: 40S and 60S are the eukaryotic subunits.

questions.stem: Which feature distinguishes helminths from protozoa?

options.B: Ability to cause disease in humans
options.C: Multicellular body with differentiated tissues and organ systems

questions.explanation: Helminths are macroscopic multicellular worms with differentiated tissues and organ systems; protozoa are microscopic single-celled eukaryotes. A: Both are eukaryotes with a true nucleus. B: Both are human pathogens. D: Chitin walls are a fungal feature. E: Both, as eukaryotes, have 80S ribosomes.

questions.stem: Fungal and bacterial cell walls differ in their main structural component. Which pairing is correct?

options.D: Fungi: no cell wall; bacteria: peptidoglycan

questions.explanation: Fungal walls contain chitin; bacterial walls contain peptidoglycan (unique to bacteria). A: Reversed. B: Cellulose is the plant cell-wall component. C: Bacteria do not use cellulose. D: Fungi do have a cell wall; animal cells are the ones without.

questions.stem: Which feature correctly distinguishes viruses from bacteria?

options.C: Viruses contain only one type of nucleic acid, DNA or RNA
options.D: Viruses grow on artificial media such as agar
options.E: Viruses have a peptidoglycan cell wall

questions.explanation: Viruses contain only DNA or RNA inside a protein capsid and are obligate intracellular. A: Viruses have no ribosomes; they use the host's. B: Bacteria divide by binary fission; viruses replicate inside cells. D: Viruses need living cells. E: Viruses have a capsid, not a cell wall.
